backlog.title: Formality Bug Fixes - Phase 1: Critical Issues
backlog.description: Fix critical bugs that prevent core PRD features from working: selectDefaultFieldProps evaluation and debounce: false immediate submission.

milestones.title: Implement selectDefaultFieldProps Evaluation
milestones.description: Implement the missing selectDefaultFieldProps evaluation at both provider and form levels, enabling dynamic default props based on form state.

tasks.title: Extend usePropsEvaluation Hook for Default Props
tasks.description: Modify the usePropsEvaluation hook to support evaluation of form-level and provider-level selectDefaultFieldProps in addition to the existing field-level selectProps.

subtasks.title: Add selectDefaultFieldProps parameters to usePropsEvaluation hook signature
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md, usePropsEvaluation hook (packages/react/src/hooks/usePropsEvaluation.ts) currently only evaluates field-level selectProps. It uses useInferredInputs for dependency inference and useWatch for isolated subscriptions.
2. INPUT: Hook receives existing selectProps parameter. Add two new parameters: formSelectDefaultFieldProps?: SelectValue<FieldProps> and providerSelectDefaultFieldProps?: SelectValue<FieldProps>. Both are SelectValue type (string or function from types/config.ts).
3. LOGIC: Extend the hook to evaluate form and provider selectDefaultFieldProps using the same expression evaluation pattern as selectProps. Use the same proxy state wrapping for field context access. Ensure evaluated props are memoized to prevent unnecessary re-evaluation.
4. OUTPUT: Return object containing evaluated formDefaultProps and providerDefaultProps (both type FieldProps), alongside existing evaluatedProps.

subtasks.title: Implement evaluation logic for form-level selectDefaultFieldProps
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From external_deps.md, expression evaluation uses evaluate() function from packages/core/src/expression/evaluate.ts with jsep parsing. The same pattern is used in usePropsEvaluation for selectProps.
2. INPUT: formSelectDefaultFieldProps parameter (SelectValue<FieldProps>) and proxyFieldStates from existing hook logic. If formSelectDefaultFieldProps is a function, it needs evaluation with field context.
3. LOGIC: Check if formSelectDefaultFieldProps is a function using typeof === 'function'. If true, call it with proxyFieldStates as argument to get evaluated props. If string, return as-is (static props). Use same memoization pattern as existing selectProps evaluation with [formSelectDefaultFieldProps, proxyFieldStates] dependencies.
4. OUTPUT: Evaluated formDefaultProps: FieldProps object to be consumed by Field component for props merging.

subtasks.title: Implement evaluation logic for provider-level selectDefaultFieldProps
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Provider-level props have lowest priority in 8-layer pipeline (codebase_analysis.md line 393). Use same evaluation pattern as form-level but with provider context.
2. INPUT: providerSelectDefaultFieldProps parameter (SelectValue<FieldProps>) and proxyFieldStates from existing hook logic.
3. LOGIC: Same evaluation logic as S2 but for provider-level props. Check if function, call with proxyFieldStates, memoize result. Ensure provider-level evaluation uses same dependency array pattern.
4. OUTPUT: Evaluated providerDefaultProps: FieldProps object to be consumed by Field component.

subtasks.title: Update TypeScript types for new hook parameters and return values
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md, SelectValue type is defined in packages/core/src/types/config.ts as polymorphic type: string | function.

3. LOGIC: Update hook function signature to include new optional parameters: formSelectDefaultFieldProps?: SelectValue<FieldProps>, providerSelectDefaultFieldProps?: SelectValue<FieldProps>. Update return type to include formDefaultProps?: FieldProps and providerDefaultProps?: FieldProps in the return object.
4. OUTPUT: Updated TypeScript function signature and return type interface. Export updated types for consumption by Field component.

milestones.title: Implement debounce: false Immediate Submission
milestones.description: Implement support for per-field debounce: false configuration to trigger immediate form submission without waiting for the debounce timer.

tasks.title: Modify Form Component to Support Immediate Submission
tasks.description: Update the Form component's changeField callback to detect when a field has debounce: false and trigger immediate submission instead of debounced submission.

subtasks.title: Add inputConfig parameter to changeField callback
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md lines 299-317, changeField callback in packages/react/src/components/Form.tsx currently only receives (name: string, value: unknown). InputConfig is needed to check debounce setting.
2. INPUT: changeField signature needs to be updated to accept InputConfig type from @formality-ui/core/types/config.ts. InputConfig.debounce property is type 'number | false'.
3. LOGIC: Update changeField callback signature from (name: string, value: unknown) to (name: string, value: unknown, inputConfig?: InputConfig). Make inputConfig optional to maintain backward compatibility.
4. OUTPUT: Updated changeField callback signature that can receive input configuration.

subtasks.title: Implement conditional execution: immediate vs debounced submit
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md, changeField always calls debouncedSubmit() (line 313). Need to add conditional logic to check inputConfig.debounce === false.
2. INPUT: inputConfig parameter from S1. Existing debouncedSubmit function and pendingChangedFields tracking.
3. LOGIC: After adding field to pendingChangedFields set, check if inputConfig?.debounce === false. If true, call submitForm() immediately (or create submitImmediate() that bypasses debounce). If false or undefined, call existing debouncedSubmit(). Ensure pendingAffectedFields logic still applies.
4. OUTPUT: Conditional submission logic that bypasses debounce when inputConfig.debounce === false.

subtasks.title: Update Field component to pass inputConfig to changeField
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Field component calls changeField via Controller's onChange. Need to find where changeField is invoked and pass inputConfig.
2. INPUT: Field component has access to inputConfig via useConfigContext. Need to pass it to changeField call.
3. LOGIC: Locate the onChange handler in Field component's Controller render prop. Find where methods.setValue (which triggers changeField) is called. Update the call to include inputConfig as third parameter. May need to create wrapper function or use useCallback to pass inputConfig.
4. OUTPUT: Field component passes inputConfig to changeField callback, enabling debounce: false detection.

subtasks.title: Ensure Form component debounce prop respects false value
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md line 136, Form component defaults debounceMs to 1000 if props.debounce is falsy. This breaks debounce: false support.
2. INPUT: Form component receives debounce prop from JSX. Type is number but should support number | false.
3. LOGIC: Update Form component props type to accept debounce?: number | false. Update the debounceMs calculation to: debounceMs = props.debounce === false ? 1000 : (props.debounce ?? 1000). This ensures false is treated specially, while undefined uses default 1000.
4. OUTPUT: Form component properly handles debounce: false prop without defaulting to 1000.

tasks.title: Add Tests for debounce: false Immediate Submission

backlog.title: Formality Bug Fixes - Phase 2: Major Issues
backlog.description: Fix major bugs related to disabled property in field states and multi-field isDisabled condition matchers.

milestones.title: Implement disabled Property in Field States
milestones.description: Populate the disabled property in field states used for condition evaluation, resolving the circular dependency issue where disabled state comes from conditions but conditions need disabled state.

tasks.title: Resolve Disabled State from Multiple Sources
tasks.description: Create a mechanism to resolve the actual disabled state for each field by combining disabled state from props, config, conditions, and groups.

subtasks.title: Create useFieldDisabledState hook to resolve disabled from all sources
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md, disabled state has 4 sources: JSX prop (<Field disabled />), field config ({ disabled: true }), condition evaluation (conditions: [{ disabled: true }]), and group state (parent FieldGroup disabled). This is HIGH complexity.
2. INPUT: Field name, field config, Field component props (JSX), form context, and group context. Need to check all four sources.
3. LOGIC: Create new hook useFieldDisabledState that checks disabled sources in priority: 1) JSX prop (props.disabled), 2) Field config disabled (fieldConfig.disabled), 3) Condition evaluation result (from useConditions), 4) Group disabled state (from GroupContext). Return resolved disabled boolean. Use useMemo with proper dependencies.
4. OUTPUT: useFieldDisabledState hook that returns disabled: boolean representing the resolved disabled state.

subtasks.title: Integrate disabled state resolution into useConditions hook
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md lines 98-119, useConditions hook builds fieldStates without disabled property. This is the bug location.
2. INPUT: useConditions hook already has access to field names via watchFields array. Need to get disabled state for each watched field.
3. LOGIC: For each field in watchFields, call useFieldDisabledState hook to get resolved disabled state. Include disabled property in the fieldStates object construction: states[fieldName] = { value: ..., isTouched: ..., disabled: useFieldDisabledState(fieldName) }. This creates a dependency cycle (conditions need disabled, disabled needs conditions) - must resolve by using PREVIOUS condition evaluation cycle's disabled result.
4. OUTPUT: fieldStates object in useConditions now includes disabled property for each field.

subtasks.title: Handle circular dependency between disabled and conditions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: CRITICAL: Circular dependency exists. Conditions evaluate disabled state, but disabled state depends on conditions. Solution: Use previous cycle's condition results or evaluate conditions in two passes.
2. INPUT: Current condition evaluation logic that needs disabled state. Disabled state sources including condition results.
3. LOGIC: Implement two-pass evaluation: Pass 1 evaluates conditions without isDisabled matcher to get base disabled state from config/props/group. Pass 2 evaluates isDisabled matcher using disabled state from Pass 1. Alternative: Use previous condition result (from last render) for isDisabled matcher in current render. Use ref to store previous condition results.
4. OUTPUT: Resolved circular dependency where isDisabled conditions use previous cycle's disabled state, avoiding infinite loop.

milestones.title: Implement Multi-Field isDisabled Condition Matcher
milestones.description: Extend the isDisabled condition matcher to work with multi-field (object) when conditions, not just single-field string when conditions.

tasks.title: Modify Condition Evaluation for Multi-Field isDisabled
tasks.description: Update the evaluateFieldMatcher and related functions to check isDisabled matcher for each field in multi-field when conditions.

subtasks.title: Move isDisabled matcher check outside string-only block
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md lines 177-199 in packages/core/src/conditions/evaluate.ts, isDisabled matcher is only checked when typeof condition.when === 'string'. This is the bug.
2. INPUT: evaluateFieldMatcher function that processes condition matchers. Current implementation has isDisabled check inside string-when block.
3. LOGIC: Extract the isDisabled matcher check logic from inside the if (typeof condition.when === 'string') block. Move it outside so it runs for both string and object when conditions. For object when, need to check isDisabled for each field in the object.
4. OUTPUT: isDisabled matcher check executes for both string and object when conditions.

subtasks.title: Implement isDisabled check for each field in object when conditions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Object when conditions have structure: { field1: { matcher1: value1 }, field2: { matcher2: value2 } }. Need to check if isDisabled matcher is present for any field.
2. INPUT: condition.when object with field names as keys and matcher objects as values. fieldStates object with disabled property for each field.
3. LOGIC: After moving isDisabled check outside string block, add logic to handle object when: Loop through each field in condition.when object. For each field, check if its matchers include isDisabled. If isDisabled matcher is present, compare it to fieldStates[fieldName].disabled. All isDisabled matchers must match (AND logic) for condition to match.
4. OUTPUT: isDisabled matcher works for multi-field conditions, checking each field's disabled state.

subtasks.title: Handle mixed matchers in multi-field conditions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Multi-field conditions can mix value matchers (is, pattern) with field state matchers (isDisabled, isValid). Example: { field1: { is: 'value' }, field2: { isDisabled: true } }.
2. INPUT: condition.when object with mixed matcher types. fieldStates for field state matchers, fieldValues for value matchers.
3. LOGIC: For each field in condition.when, determine which matcher type is present. Value matchers use fieldValues[fieldName] for comparison. Field state matchers (isDisabled, isValid) use fieldStates[fieldName] for comparison. Combine results with AND logic - all matchers must match for condition to match.
4. OUTPUT: Multi-field conditions correctly evaluate mixed value and field state matchers.

backlog.title: Formality Bug Fixes - Phase 3: Medium Priority Issues
backlog.description: Fix medium priority issues related to memory leaks, type safety, and race conditions.

milestones.title: Fix Memory Leak in Subscription Cleanup
milestones.description: Improve subscription cleanup in useSubscriptions hook to prevent orphaned subscriptions during rapid subscription changes.

tasks.title: Improve Subscription Tracking and Cleanup
tasks.description: Implement more robust subscription tracking that ensures only subscriptions from the current effect invocation are cleaned up.

subtasks.title: Add per-effect subscription tracking in useSubscriptions
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md, useSubscriptions hook in packages/react/src/hooks/useSubscriptions.ts manages field subscriptions. Current cleanup may not handle rapid changes properly.
2. INPUT: Current useSubscriptions implementation with useEffect cleanup function. Subscriptions are added to inverted index.
3. LOGIC: Use useRef to track subscriptions added in current effect invocation: const currentSubscriptionsRef = useRef<Set<string>>(new Set()). When adding subscription, add to currentSubscriptionsRef. In cleanup, only remove subscriptions that are in currentSubscriptionsRef. Clear the ref at start of effect. This ensures cleanup only removes subscriptions added in this invocation.
4. OUTPUT: Robust subscription cleanup that prevents orphaned subscriptions during rapid changes.

subtasks.title: Add cleanup ordering guarantees
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: Ensure cleanup happens in correct order when dependencies change rapidly.
2. INPUT: useEffect with subscription dependencies.
3. LOGIC: Ensure cleanup function runs before new subscriptions are added (default React behavior). Document the cleanup order in comments. Consider adding useEffect cleanup logging in development mode to help debug subscription issues.
4. OUTPUT: Guaranteed cleanup ordering with documentation.

milestones.title: Improve Type Safety in Expression Evaluation
milestones.description: Add type checking before arithmetic operations in expression evaluation to handle non-numeric values gracefully.

tasks.title: Add Type Guards for Arithmetic Operations
tasks.description: Implement type checking before arithmetic operations to prevent runtime errors with non-numeric values.

subtasks.title: Add type checking before arithmetic operations in evaluate function
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: From codebase_analysis.md lines 104-130 in packages/core/src/expression/evaluate.ts, arithmetic operations assume number type. Need to add type guards.
2. INPUT: Binary expression node with operator (+, -, *, /, %) and left/right operands. Evaluation context.
3. LOGIC: Before performing arithmetic, check if both operands are numbers using typeof === 'number' && !Number.isNaN(operand). If not numbers, return undefined or handle gracefully. For + operator, if either operand is string, perform string concatenation instead of addition. Document the type coercion behavior.
4. OUTPUT: Arithmetic operations that handle non-numeric values gracefully without throwing errors.

subtasks.title: Add type handling for null and undefined values
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: null and undefined should be handled consistently in arithmetic.
2. INPUT: Operands that may be null or undefined.
3. LOGIC: If operand is null or undefined, treat as 0 for arithmetic operations (or return undefined). Document the chosen behavior. Consider making this configurable if different use cases need different handling. For now, return undefined for arithmetic with null/undefined to fail safely.
4. OUTPUT: Consistent handling of null/undefined in arithmetic expressions.

tasks.title: Add Type Safety Tests
tasks.description: Write tests to verify expression evaluation handles type mismatches gracefully.
